claims.text: LPBF with in-situ monitoring can form RHEA/Cu composite structures at large scale.
LPBF with in-situ monitoring can produce a stable microstructure in RHEA/Cu composites.
LPBF provides precise control of thermal conditions.
In-situ monitoring permits real-time observation of the reaction.
The proposed starting materials are RHEA and Cu powders.
Controlled thermal gradients and in-situ monitoring are required under the proposed high-temperature processing conditions.
The intervention forms a stable interface between RHEAs and Cu.
Precise control of thermal conditions enables a stable RHEA/Cu interface despite their significant positive heat of mixing.
LPBF with in-situ monitoring will increase microstructural stability by 30% relative to traditional methods.
The proposed increase in microstructural stability will be reflected by reduced defects and porosity.
Mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering are traditional comparison methods for forming these composite structures.
A processing temperature of 1000–1200 °C is required to achieve the desired microstructure.
A laser power density of 500–700 W/cm² is required to achieve the desired microstructure.
Optimal LPBF parameters may vary with the specific RHEA and Cu compositions.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if LPBF with in-situ monitoring fails to produce at least a 20% increase in microstructural stability relative to traditional methods.
